title: Which order do these four lists of decimals take, greatest first?
description: Four lists of five decimals, two with units, are arranged from greatest to smallest by writing equal places and comparing from the left, the same way as the example in the book.
teaching_notes: One idea: write the same places, then compare from the left. Watch for children who think more digits make a greater number.

source: Figure it Out (end of chapter), Q4
video_script.why: The child has compared pairs of decimals and now orders whole lists of five.
video_script.substitution: Write every number with the same places, then compare from the left to put them in order.
video_script.anchor: Four lists of five decimals each: plain numbers, then grams, then metres.
video_script.payoff_line: Compare from the left, and the first difference decides the order

final_answer.spoken: first list, eleven point one zero, eleven point zero one, one point one zero one, one point zero one one, one point zero one; second list, two point seven six eight, two point six nine eight, two point six seven five, two point five six seven, two point four nine nine; third list, four point six seven eight grams, four point six six six grams, four point six five six grams, four point six zero zero grams, four point five nine five grams; fourth list, thirty three point three three one metres, thirty three point three one three metres, thirty three point three one metres, thirty three point one three three metres, thirty three point one three metres

maths_rules: (b) tenths 5,6,7,4,6; 2.768, then 2.698 > 2.675 on hundredths, then 2.567, then 2.499
(c) hundredths 7,6,5,0 for 4.678, 4.666, 4.656, 4.600; 4.595 has tenths 5 so is last
check: each number is less than the one before it, in every list
video_script.design: The four lists stay on the board. Each is rewritten with the same number of places, and the order builds underneath it.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; four lists of five decimals each

marks.ask: an arrow from greatest to smallest appears

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='lists'/>Four lists of numbers are given, with five numbers in each.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Arrange every list from the greatest to the smallest.

beats.on_screen: the four lists stay on the board
narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: write the same places; compare from the left; the first difference decides

marks.same: the example in the book appears beside this question
marks.left: an arrow runs from left to right

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>We solve this the same way as the example in your book.
<bookmark mark='fill'/>Write every number with the same places after the point.
<bookmark mark='left'/>Then compare from the left, and the first difference decides.

beats.on_screen: Given: four lists of five numbers; the third list in grams, the fourth in metres
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, four lists of five numbers each.
<bookmark mark='units'/>The third list is in grams, and the fourth is in metres.

beats.on_screen: To find: each list in descending order
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to arrange each list from greatest to smallest.

marks.a1: the first list is rewritten with three places
marks.a2: the two numbers with a tens digit move to the front
marks.a3: the other three are placed in order

narration: <bookmark mark='a1'/>Step one, the first list. Write each number with three places after the point.
<bookmark mark='a2'/>Eleven point one zero zero and eleven point zero one zero have a tens digit. They come first.
<bookmark mark='a3'/>Among the rest, one point one zero one is greatest. Then come one point zero one one and one point zero one zero.

marks.b2: the first and last numbers are placed

narration: <bookmark mark='b1'/>Step two, the second list. The units are all two, so compare the tenths.
<bookmark mark='b2'/>Seven is greatest, so two point seven six eight is first. Four is least, so two point four nine nine is last.
<bookmark mark='b3'/>Two point six nine eight beats two point six seven five on the hundredths. Two point five six seven comes after them.

beats.on_screen: (c) all 4 units; hundredths 7, 6, 5, 0 for 4.678, 4.666, 4.656, 4.600; 4.595 has tenths 5, so last

marks.c2: the number with tenths five moves to the end
marks.c3: the hundredths column is boxed and the four numbers are placed

narration: <bookmark mark='c1'/>Step three, the third list, in grams. The units are all four.
<bookmark mark='c2'/>Four point five nine five has tenths five, while the rest have six, so it is last.
<bookmark mark='c3'/>For the others, the hundredths are seven, six, five and zero, which gives the order.

marks.d1: the fourth list is rewritten with three places
marks.d2: the three numbers with tenths three are placed
marks.d3: the two numbers with tenths one are placed

narration: <bookmark mark='d1'/>Step four, the fourth list, in metres. Write every length with three places after the point.
<bookmark mark='d2'/>Thirty three point three three one is first. Then come thirty three point three one three and thirty three point three one zero.
<bookmark mark='d3'/>Thirty three point one three three comes next, and thirty three point one three zero is last.

beats.on_screen: check: each number is less than the one before it, in every list

marks.chk: a tick appears between each pair of neighbours

narration: <bookmark mark='chk'/>Step five, check each list from left to right. Every number is smaller than the one before it.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Compare from the left, and the first difference decides the order.
<bookmark mark='la'/>First list. Eleven point one zero, eleven point zero one, one point one zero one.
<bookmark mark='la2'/>Then one point zero one one, and one point zero one.
<bookmark mark='lb'/>Second list. Two point seven six eight, two point six nine eight, two point six seven five.
<bookmark mark='lb2'/>Then two point five six seven, and two point four nine nine.
<bookmark mark='lc'/>Third list. Four point six seven eight, four point six six six, four point six five six.
<bookmark mark='lc2'/>Then four point six zero zero, and four point five nine five grams.
<bookmark mark='ld'/>Fourth list. Thirty three point three three one, thirty three point three one three.
<bookmark mark='ld2'/>Then thirty three point three one, and thirty three point one three three.
<bookmark mark='ld3'/>Last, thirty three point one three metres.
